analysis.analysis: A named external paper composed at its press's grain: the figures kept, the authors and the conditions dropped, a verdict added. The loss is dimensional, in claim boundary: the power limit's scope and the classification's status do not reach the composition. Scalar PER sees the authors lost; the boundary loss is in the findings.
analysis.d: THE ATA PAPER BY ITS TITLE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-06: 'Astronomers using the SETI Institute's Allen Telescope Array searched the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS for artificial radio technosignatures and found no evidence of alien technology.' Under 'Key Details of the Study': 7.25 hours over five sessions, 1 to 9 GHz, 'The automated `bliss` pipeline detected ~74 million narrowband signals. After RFI (radio frequency interference) frequency and drift-rate blanking, this was reduced to ~2 million candidates, and further filtered down to 211 hits via `NBeamAnalysis` for visual inspection.' Results: 'Every single candidate signal was traced back to local human-made Earth technology, satellites, or interference—yielding zero artificial signals originating from the object.' Power: 'The non-detection rules out any active radio transmitters stronger than roughly 10 to 110 Watts on or near 3I/ATLAS.' Conclusion: 'the data firmly reinforces that 3I/ATLAS is a natural comet.' Seven source cards: arXiv, IOPscience (The Astronomical Journal), Phys.org, Berkeley SETI, Universe Today, Sci.News, Space.
analysis.d_full: THE ATA PAPER BY ITS TITLE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-06: 'Astronomers using the SETI Institute's Allen Telescope Array searched the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS for artificial radio technosignatures and found no evidence of alien technology.' Under 'Key Details of the Study': 7.25 hours over five sessions, 1 to 9 GHz, 'The automated `bliss` pipeline detected ~74 million narrowband signals. After RFI (radio frequency interference) frequency and drift-rate blanking, this was reduced to ~2 million candidates, and further filtered down to 211 hits via `NBeamAnalysis` for visual inspection.' Results: 'Every single candidate signal was traced back to local human-made Earth technology, satellites, or interference—yielding zero artificial signals originating from the object.' Power: 'The non-detection rules out any active radio transmitters stronger than roughly 10 to 110 Watts on or near 3I/ATLAS.' Conclusion: 'the data firmly reinforces that 3I/ATLAS is a natural comet.' Seven source cards: arXiv, IOPscience (The Astronomical Journal), Phys.org, Berkeley SETI, Universe Today, Sci.News, Space.
findings: WHAT IS ACCURATE. The campaign's figures are the paper's: 7.25 hours over five sessions, 1 to 9 GHz, 'The automated `bliss` pipeline detected ~74 million narrowband signals. After RFI (radio frequency interference) frequency and drift-rate blanking, this was reduced to ~2 million candidates, and further filtered down to 211 hits via `NBeamAnalysis` for visual inspection.' The IOPscience card quotes the abstract's first sentence ('Jun 3, 2026 — In this campaign, we used the SETI Institute's Allen Telescope Array to observe 3I/ATLAS from 1–9 GHz.').

THE CLASSIFICATION RENDERED AS A TRACING. 'Every single candidate signal was traced back to local human-made Earth technology, satellites, or interference—yielding zero artificial signals originating from the object.' The procedure classifies: it removes hits by rule and rejects the inspected events as interference. The notebook on the paper's own two illustrated rejections (#1742 §5.2): 'The published sentence ("every single one turned out to be human-made interference") states an identification where the procedure supplies a classification.' The step past the paper's classification is the press's: the Sci.News card reads 'All traced back to technology on the surface of the Earth or our own Earth-orbiting satellites.', and the Space card carries the same wording. The Overview copies it into the paper's account (repaired 2026-11-06 on the ata-3i-atlas-search composer's report).

THE LIMIT WITHOUT ITS SCOPE. 'The non-detection rules out any active radio transmitters stronger than roughly 10 to 110 Watts on or near 3I/ATLAS.' The paper's abstract ties its limit ("an effective isotropic radiated power upper limit of 10-110 W") to the frequencies and drift rates its survey kept. The composition's sentence takes the SETI Institute's statement as the Sci.News and Space cards carry it ('The observations place upper limits on the power of any radio transmitter on or near 3I/ATLAS, ruling out signals stronger than about 10-110 W — approximately the power of a household appliance — over the detected frequencies.'), drops its closing 'over the detected frequencies' and adds 'active' (repaired 2026-11-06). The drift range is the filter the notebook reads (#1742 §5.1): '"We filter our hits for drift rates between 0.05–1.5 Hz/s at all frequencies." The text gives no sign. Figure 4 does: its "Drift Rate Range Hits" occupy 0 to +1.5 Hz/s on the signed axis and none of the negative half.' And the physics: 'A rising range-rate lowers the received frequency, so a positive acceleration gives a negative drift.' A transmitter on the object, drifting negative, sits in the half the filter removed, so the composition's 'any active radio transmitters ... on or near 3I/ATLAS' covers exactly the class the stated method could not see.

A VERDICT THE SEARCH DOES NOT REACH. 'the data firmly reinforces that 3I/ATLAS is a natural comet.' The Phys.org card carries the press's version ('the study sets new constraints reinforcing that 3I/ATLAS is a natural object'). A nondetection of narrowband technosignatures above a power limit bears on transmitters; the object's cometary nature is established by its spectroscopy and its OH lines. 'Firmly' is the composition's own.

NO AUTHOR, THE STAGE BLURRED. The paper's fifteen authors (Sheikh, Garcia Lopez, Gerrard, Davenport, Farah and others) are absent; the institution and the array stand for them. 'Drift-rate blanking' is the paper's own term ('After drift-rate blanking, ∼2 million hits remained.'), and the paper's own summary sentences leave the signed interval unnamed as well; the composition carries that naming, and the stage the notebook questions has no sign in either (repaired 2026-11-06).

SMALLEST REPAIR. 'No narrowband signal above 10–110 W was found within 1–9 GHz and the drift rates the search retained (0.05–1.5 Hz/s, positive); 211 inspected events were classified as interference.' COUNTERTEST: rerun '3i atlas ata drift rate filter' (seated 2026-11-04) and record whether the sign appears.

analysis.reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the paper by its title, the Overview reports its campaign at the paper's own figures: the hours, the sessions, the band, the pipeline's names and the counts at each stage, and the power limit. Those figures are right. Read against the paper and the notebook, the composition does three things the paper does not: it turns a classification of 211 inspected events into an identification of their origin, it states the power limit without the frequencies and drift rates it is conditioned on, and it closes on a verdict about the object's nature that a technosignature nondetection does not reach. It names no author, and the drift interval, the one stage whose sign the notebook finds reversed, is folded into 'drift-rate blanking'.
